neighbours.label: unclear; best guess is a list, not one pattern: (a) the object of a verb of killing or saving ('to kill you', 'kill Jesus', 'saving the world') and (b) the name of a biocidal salt (copper sulfate, sodium azide). The + pole fires on revenge / avenge
fire: The queen feared that her own brother had paid a stranger to kill her.
The soldiers were ordered to find the rebel leader and kill him.
The hero rested for a week after saving the city again.
The plotters met at night and agreed on a plan to kill Caesar.
Treat the pond with copper sulfate to keep the algae down.
The lab stores its antibodies in buffer with sodium azide.
Gardeners once sprayed lead arsenate on apple trees.
The pool was disinfected with calcium hypochlorite every morning.
quiet: The queen hoped that her own brother had paid a stranger to guide her.
The soldiers were ordered to find the village elder and thank him.
The hero rested for a week after visiting the city again.
The senators met at night and agreed on a plan to praise Caesar.
Season the stew with sea salt to bring the flavour out.
The kitchen stores its bread in a tin with baking soda.
Gardeners once spread wood ash on apple trees.
The pool was filled with fresh spring water every morning.

notes: Weak pole (max 5.69). Probes: copper sulfate 0.62, sodium azide 0.46, 'kill you' 0.42, 'saving the world' 0.39, 'slay the dragon' 0.34, 'kill Jesus' 0.32; but controls are close: 'feed the dragon' 0.30, 'guard you' 0.23, table salt 0.19, tuna 0.36, 'punches the ape and' 0.36. I could not find what the two groups share, so the list is kept and said to be a list. Expected to fail or be borderline.
